person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We advocate for pushing further the integration of machine learning and combinatorial optimization and detail a methodology to do so.

span.label: machine learning for combinatorial optimization
span.quote: We survey different uses of ML to help solve combinatorial optimization problems and organize them along two orthogonal axes.

span.label: review
span.quote: This paper surveys the recent attempts, both from the machine learning and operations research communities, at leveraging machine learning to solve combinatorial optimization problems.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: HANDCRAFTED HEURISTICS ARE SAID TO FILL TWO DIFFERENT GAPS, AND ONE OF THEM IS DEFINITIONAL: state-of-the-art algorithms rely on handcrafted heuristics for decisions that are otherwise TOO EXPENSIVE TO COMPUTE **OR MATHEMATICALLY NOT WELL DEFINED**. The craft is standing in both for intractability and for the absence of a definition, and the two are named in one breath
span.quote: Given the hard nature of these problems, state-of-the-art algorithms rely on handcrafted heuristics for making decisions that are otherwise too expensive to compute or mathematically not well defined. Thus, machine learning looks like a natural candidate to make such decisions in a more principled and optimized way.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A FIELD IS INTRODUCED WITH TWO NAMES IN ITS FIRST SENTENCE: operations research, ALSO REFERRED TO AS PRESCRIPTIVE ANALYTICS, started in the second world war as an initiative to use mathematics and computer science to assist military planners. One discipline, two labels, and the second belongs to a different literature
span.note: about this quote: RE-SLICED. The acceptance footnote and licence notice are spliced INTO this sentence - "to use mathematics and computer science * Accepted to the European Journal of Operations Research. c(cid:13)2020. Licensed under the Creative Commons cbnd 1 to assist military planners" - so it cannot be quoted whole. The naming is at its head. `c(cid:13)` is a copyright symbol that failed to map.
span.quote: Operations research, also referred to as prescriptive analytics, started in the second world war as an initiative to use mathematics and computer science

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE PAPER'S MAIN MOVE IS A RE-DESCRIPTION OF ITS OBJECTS AS SOMETHING ELSE: a main point is SEEING GENERIC OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS AS DATA POINTS, and then INQUIRING WHAT IS THE RELEVANT DISTRIBUTION OF PROBLEMS to use for learning on a given task. Problems become instances drawn from a distribution, and that shift is the contribution
span.quote: A main point of the paper is seeing generic optimization problems as data points and inquiring what is the relevant distribution of problems to use for learning on a given task.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN APPARENT CONTRADICTION BETWEEN A COMPLEXITY CLASS AND PRACTICE IS POSED AS THE PAPER'S OPENING QUESTION: for these problems IT IS CONSIDERED UNLIKELY that a polynomial-time algorithm exists - HOWEVER, IN PRACTICE, the algorithms solve instances with up to millions of variables and constraints - HOW IS IT POSSIBLE TO SOLVE NP-HARD PROBLEMS IN PRACTICAL TIME? The category and the practice disagree, and the disagreement is the subject
span.quote: This is bad news, in the sense that, for those problems, it is considered unlikely that an algorithm whose running time is polynomial in the size of the input exists. However, in practice, CO algorithms can solve instances with up to millions of decision variables and constraints. How is it possible to solve NP-hard problems in practical time?

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHAT IS TO BE AUTOMATED IS DESCRIBED AS UNWRITTEN, AND A PARENTHESIS CONCEDES IT MAY NOT EXIST: the aim is TO AUGMENT AND AUTOMATE THE UNWRITTEN EXPERT INTUITION **(OR LACK OF)** on various existing algorithms. Three words in brackets admit that the target of the automation might be absent, and the sentence continues as though it were not in doubt
span.quote: Rather, it aims to augment and automate the unwritten expert intuition (or lack of) on various existing algorithms. Given that these problems are highly structured, we believe it is relevant to augment solving algorithms with machine learning – and especially deep learning to address the high dimensionality of such problems.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A DEFINITION IS DECLINED FOR THREE TRACTABILITY REASONS AND NONE OF THEM IS IMPOSSIBILITY: explicitly defining what makes an instance A LIKELY ONE for the company IS TEDIOUS, DOES NOT SCALE, AND IT IS NOT CLEAR HOW IT CAN BE LEVERAGED when writing the algorithm - so the definition is replaced by a wish to AUTOMATICALLY SPECIALIZE. **The reasons for not defining are practical, and the paper says so plainly**
span.quote: Explicitly defining what makes a TSP a likely one for the company is tedious, does not scale, and it is not clear how it can be leveraged when explicitly writing an optimization algorithm. We would like to automatically specialize TSP algorithms for this company.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: HUMAN TRIAL-AND-ERROR IS NAMED AS A LEAKAGE CHANNEL, WHICH IS WHY A COMPARISON NEEDS INDEPENDENT DATA: as for ALL such algorithms, A FAIR COMPARISON can only be done on AN INDEPENDENT DATASET of instances - BECAUSE THROUGH HUMAN TRIALS AND ERRORS, THE DATA USED WHEN BUILDING THE ALGORITHM LEAKS INTO THE DESIGN OF THE ALGORITHM, even without explicit training. **The designer is a fitting procedure**
span.note: about this quote: RE-SLICED, AND MY OWN CUT-WORD GUARD IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. My first end key was "...even without e" - which is where a 240-character DEBUG PRINT had truncated the sentence while I was searching the file. **I used the output of my own truncated display as a key.** The guard refused it, and the real text is "even without explicit learning components". Slice from the FILE, never from a print of the file.
span.quote: However, as for all CO algorithms, a fair comparison to another algorithm can only be done on an independent dataset of instances, as in (4). This is because through human trials and errors, the data used when building the algorithm leaks into the design of the algorithm

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE BASELINE IS SHOWN TO SHARE THE WEAKNESS BEING CHARGED AGAINST THE NEW METHOD: learned algorithms may be expected to FAIL ON UNSEEN INSTANCES TOO FAR FROM TRAINING - and IT IS ALSO WORTH NOTING that TRADITIONAL algorithms MIGHT NOT EVEN WORK CONSISTENTLY across all instances of a problem family, but TEND TO BE MORE ADAPTED TO PARTICULAR STRUCTURES. The complaint turns out to describe the incumbent as well
span.quote: and so we may expect CO algorithms that leverage ML models to fail when evaluated on unseen problem instances that are too far from what has been used for training the ML predictor. As previously motivated, it is also worth noting that traditional CO algorithms might not even work consistently across all possible instances of a problem family, but rather tend to be more adapted to particular structures of problems

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A STANDING DIFFICULTY IS ATTRIBUTED TO A FUZZY DISTINCTION BETWEEN TWO DESCRIPTIONS OF ONE THING: generalization REMAINS A CHALLENGING TOPIC, PROBABLY BECAUSE OF THE FUZZY DISTINCTION BETWEEN A MULTI-TASK SETTING AND A LARGE ENVIRONMENT ENCOMPASSING ALL OF THE TASKS. The obstacle is not a missing result but an unresolved choice of description
span.quote: Generalization in RL remains a challenging topic, probably because of the fuzzy distinction between a multi-task setting, and a large environment encompassing all of the tasks.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE GRANULARITY OF A CATEGORY IS PRESENTED AS A DECISION WITH NO PRINCIPLED ANSWER, AND THE EXAMPLE IS CONCRETE: CHOOSING HOW AMBITIOUS ONE SHOULD BE IN DEFINING THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE DISTRIBUTION IS A HARD QUESTION - if the company expands to other cities, SHOULD THEY BE CONSIDERED AS SEPARATE DISTRIBUTIONS, and one policy learned per city? Where one category ends and the next begins is a question the framework does not answer
span.note: about this quote: EXTENDED: the first cut stopped before "and learn one branching policy per city?", which the tag depends on - the question mark carries the whole force of the point.
span.quote: Choosing how ambitious one should be in defining the characteristics of the distribution is a hard question. For instance, if the Montreal company expands its business to other cities, should they be considered as separate distributions, and learn one branching policy per

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SURVEY'S OWN CATEGORIES ARE DISCLAIMED AS NEITHER DISJOINT NOR EXHAUSTIVE, WHILE BEING USED: the sections ARE NOT NECESSARILY DISJOINT NOR EXHAUSTIVE BUT ARE A NATURAL WAY TO LOOK AT THE LITERATURE. A taxonomy offered with its two standard failure modes conceded and the word NATURAL doing the justifying
span.quote: sections are not necessarily disjoint nor exhaustive but are a natural way to look at the literature.

span.label: in imitation-learning settings, performance is bounded by the (possibly suboptimal) expert
span.note: what this limits: every imitation-learning result: THE PERFORMANCE OF THE LEARNED POLICY IS BOUNDED BY THE EXPERT - it cannot exceed what it imitates
span.quote: the performance of the learned policy is bounded by the expert

span.label: learned algorithms may not generalize to unseen problem instances
span.note: what this limits: any generalisation claim: the learned algorithm MAY NOT WORK PROPERLY ON OTHER INSTANCES FROM THE TRUE PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION
span.quote: may not work properly on other instances from the true probability distribution

span.label: The literature surveyed is early-stage rather than mature, so the survey reports directions rather than settled algorithms.
span.note: what this limits: the standing of the survey's conclusions: THE LITERATURE WE SURVEY IS EXPLORATORY, I.E., WE AIM AT HIGHLIGHTING PROMISING RESEARCH DIRECTIONS ... INSTEAD OF RE[porting settled results]
span.quote: In light of the current state of the field, the literature we survey is exploratory, i.e., we aim at highlighting promising research directions in the use of ML within CO, instead of reporting on already mature algorithms.

span.label: Unsupervised learning is excluded from the survey.
span.note: what this limits: the coverage of the survey: unsupervised learning is excluded
span.quote: Because unsupervised learning has received so far little attention in conjunction with CO and its immediate use seems difficult, we are not discussing it any further.

span.label: The treatment of imitation learning is a simplification of the ML literature.
span.note: what this limits: the imitation-learning material as a guide to that literature: THE PART OF IMITATION LEARNING PRESENTED HERE IS LIMITED COMPARED TO THE CURRENT LITERATURE IN ML
span.quote: The part of imitation learning presented here is limited compared to the current literature in ML.

span.label: Choosing which learning algorithm will perform best is outside the scope of the proposed methodology.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the methodology to choose between algorithms: IDENTIFYING WHICH ALGORITHM WILL PERFORM BEST IS AN OPEN RESEARCH QUESTION UNLIKELY TO HAVE A SIMPLE ANSWER, AND IS OUTSIDE OF THE SCOPE OF THE METHODOLOGY PRESENTED HERE
span.quote: In general, identifying which algorithm will perform best is an open research question unlikely to have a simple answer, and is outside of the scope of the methodology presented here.

span.label: The expert decisions the learned models are fitted to are stated to be, in part, mathematically not well defined.
span.note: what this limits: a learned replacement for a solver heuristic: the decisions in question are ones that are either too expensive to compute or mathematically not well defined, so for some of them there is no formal target the model could be right or wrong about
span.quote: state-of-the-art algorithms rely on handcrafted heuristics for making decisions that are otherwise too expensive to compute or mathematically not well defined

span.label: The distribution the method is supposed to learn cannot be characterised, so a finite set of collected instances silently becomes the definition of the problem class.
span.note: what this limits: a claim that a learned CO algorithm solves a problem class: the true distribution is unknown and cannot be characterised explicitly, so what is learned is whatever a finite collected set - for instance a company's historical instances - happens to contain
span.quote: This is unknown, and cannot even be mathematically characterized in an explicit way. Because we do not know what is in this distribution, we can only learn an algorithm that performs well on a finite set of TSPs sampled from this distribution (for instance, a set of historical instances collected by the company), thus implicitly incorporating the desired information about the distribution of instances

span.label: The quantity that defines success is stated to be inaccessible, and every reported figure is an estimate of it on held-out data.
span.note: what this limits: any reported generalization error: the objective it estimates remains inaccessible, so the number is the model's performance on a particular held-out set and not the property itself
span.quote: Because (1) remains inaccessible, we estimate the generalization error by evaluating the trained model on a separate test dataset
